lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Three Topics in Two Minutes
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernanda Bassani Rubio | Lesson 9 -- Three Topics in Two Minutes
lesson.grammar_point: should and shouldnt for advice and recommendations

listenings.text: Good morning, everyone. I have three topics today. First of all, our results. Sales increased by six percent this quarter, and we reached ninety-eight percent of the target. Moving on to the second topic: new customers. We visited five new customers, and two of them placed an order. And to sum up, my recommendation. I think we should visit our two biggest customers every month, not every quarter. They buy more when we visit them. Thank you. Any questions?

Many suppliers present to me every year, so I have some advice. First, you should be short. Ten minutes is enough. Nobody wants a presentation of one hour. Second, you shouldn't read the slides. I can read. I want to hear you. And your English does not need to be perfect. My English is not perfect! It should be clear. Third, you should always say your recommendation at the end, clearly. What do you want me to do? Tell me. That is a good presentation for me.
